reference: util-linux flock is the independent oracle for private regular-file operations, explicit sysexits statuses, bounded child commands and all file effects. Metadata contracts use the documented Bash builtin interface. Installed manual specifies sysexits; isolated reference discoveries preserve error precedence.
coverage: Bash reports flock as a builtin with type -t.
Bash help contains the documented FD and file command forms and principal options.
Bash short help exposes the registered synopsis.
The loadable's documented version metadata is stable.
Private-file FD lifetime/unlock, shared and exclusive conflicts, bounded waits, file command effects/status, close/no-fork modes and parser/open errors.
Explicit usage64, bad-descriptor65, open66 and negative-wait71 statuses, with parser/open/timer precedence.
Command arity, numeric filename versus lone descriptor selection, and no unintended creation or child effects after argument errors.
Same-shell recovery after negative waits and invalid command modes.
Guest pass 9 (G131): -F keeps the calling shell, the command holds the lock, --verbose, --fcntl, long-option forms and util-linux wording/statuses.
exclusions: Only ordinary private regular files, private inherited descriptors, bounded conflicts and short /bin/sh children are qualified. No cross-host locking, host lock files, filesystem stress, process signaling or nonlocal filesystem behavior.
Release-before-deadline synchronization, arbitrary inherited-descriptor observations, terminal/native process effects and fault injection remain unqualified.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash registers flock as a builtin using the Bash type -t contract.
cases.script: type -t flock

cases.purpose: Check the full Bash help text against the pinned documented forms, option spellings, and conflict behavior without invoking a lock operation.
cases.script:
h=$(help flock) || exit 1
[[ $h == *"Manage advisory file locks via flock(2)."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FD"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE command [args...]"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *'flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] FILE -c "shell command"'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--shared"* && $h == *"--exclusive"* && $h == *"--unlock"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--nonblock"* && $h == *"--wait"* && $h == *"--conflict-exit-code"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $h == *"--close"* && $h == *"--no-fork"* && $h == *"--command"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'documented-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check Bash help -s output against the synopsis registered in flock_struct.short_doc and Bash help builtin formatting.
cases.script: help -s flock
cases.stdout: flock: flock [-sxun] [-w SECONDS] [-E N] FD | FILE [command [args] | -c CMD]

cases.purpose: Check the loadable's documented version response; --version exits before opening an operand or acquiring a lock.
cases.script: flock --version

cases.purpose: Compare FD lock lifetime, independent-open conflict and explicit unlock using a private file.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -xn 8
if flock -xn 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'held=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9
printf 'released
'

cases.purpose: Compare compatible shared locks and configured exclusive conflict status on separate private open descriptions.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -sn 8
flock -sn 9
if flock -xn -E 23 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'exclusive=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9

cases.purpose: A small bounded timed conflict returns the configured status, then acquisition succeeds after release.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
flock -xn 8
if flock -x -w 0.02 -E 24 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'timeout=%s
' "$rc"
flock -u 8
flock -x -w 0.02 9
flock -u 9

cases.purpose: Compare private lock-file creation, shell command effects, exit status and release after child completion.
cases.script:
if flock lock -c 'printf "payload\n" > result; exit 7'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'child=%s\n' "$rc"
flock -n lock -c 'printf "released\n"'

cases.purpose: Compare close/no-fork command modes and incompatible options on private files; no-fork runs in a disposable subshell.
cases.script:
flock -o lock -c 'printf close > closed'
if (flock -F lock -c 'printf nofork > direct; exit 9'); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'nofork=%s\n' "$rc"
if flock -Fo lock -c 'printf forbidden > unexpected'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'incompatible=%s\n' "$rc"
[[ ! -e unexpected ]]

cases.purpose: Compare malformed-option and missing-parent open errors, retaining diagnostics and creation effects.
cases.script:
for arg in bad ''; do
 if flock -w "$arg" lock; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf 'timeout=%s\n' "$rc"
done
if flock -E 256 lock; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'exit-code=%s\n' "$rc"
if flock missing/lock -c 'printf unexpected'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'open=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare the actual negative-timeout error status on an uncontended private descriptor, including reference timer setup errors, without assuming parser behavior.
cases.script:
exec 9>lock
if flock -w -1 9; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf "negative-wait=%s\n" "$rc"

cases.purpose: Reject missing operands with explicit util-linux usage status.
cases.script: flock

cases.purpose: A closed private descriptor reports data-error65.
cases.script:
exec 8>&-
flock 8

cases.purpose: A nonnegative descriptor outside the int range is a usage failure before any lock attempt.
A lone nonnumeric operand is an invalid descriptor and must not create a file.
cases.script: flock untouched

cases.purpose: Reject extra arguments after FILE -c CMD before file creation or child execution.
cases.script: flock target -c 'printf forbidden > marker' extra

cases.purpose: Reject extra operands with prefix -c without creating or executing anything.
cases.script: flock -c 'printf forbidden > marker' target extra

cases.purpose: With a command, an all-digit operand names a private file rather than a descriptor.
cases.script: flock 12 -c 'printf numeric > marker'

cases.purpose: Finite negative wait reports timer-error71 even when -n is also specified.
cases.script:
exec 9>lock
flock -n -w -1 9

cases.purpose: A missing-parent open error66 precedes negative-wait timer setup.
cases.script: flock -w -1 missing/lock -c 'printf forbidden > marker'

cases.purpose: Negative-wait timer setup precedes closed-descriptor locking, without installing any timer in the embedding shell.
cases.script:
exec 8>&-
flock -w -1 8

cases.purpose: A valid file form opens its private file before negative-wait timer failure and never runs the child.
cases.script: flock -w -1 lock -c 'printf forbidden > marker'

cases.purpose: After caught negative-wait and incompatible-mode errors, preserve descriptor ownership, leave no lock/child effects, and execute a later valid file command in the same shell.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
exec 9>lock
if flock -w -1 -E 23 8; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 71 ]]
flock -xn 9
flock -u 9
if flock -Fo untouched -c 'printf forbidden > marker'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 64 && ! -e untouched && ! -e marker ]]
flock -n -w 0 lock -c 'printf recovered > result'
printf 'recovered\n'

cases.purpose: G131: -F runs the command without a waiting flock process, but the calling script must continue afterwards with the command's status, and the lock is released when the command ends.
cases.script:
if flock -F lock -c 'printf nofork > direct; exit 9'; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'nofork=%s\n' "$rc"
flock -F lock true
printf 'after\n'
cat direct; echo
flock -n lock true
printf 'released\n'

cases.purpose: G131: with -F the command itself holds the lock: a second non-blocking flock run by the command conflicts, and the shell survives in a command substitution too.
cases.script:
if flock -F lock flock -n -E 7 lock true; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'inner=%s\n' "$rc"
out=$(flock -F lock true; echo still)
printf '%s\n' "$out"

cases.purpose: G131: --verbose reports the lock wait and the command on stdout after the command's own output when stdout is a pipe; the fd form reports the wait; -F prints no report to a pipe.
cases.script:
flock --verbose lock echo hi | sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}/T/'
flock --verbose lock -c 'echo c' | sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}/T/'
exec 9>lock
flock --verbose 9 | sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}/T/'
flock -u 9
flock --verbose -F lock true | wc -c
flock --verb -u lock echo unlocked | sed -E 's/[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}/T/'

cases.purpose: G131: --verbose explains a non-blocking conflict and a timed-out wait on stderr; the conflict exit code is unchanged.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
flock 8
flock --verbose -n lock true || echo rc=$?
flock --verbose -w 0.01 -E 4 lock true || echo rc=$?
flock --verbose -w 0 lock true || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: G131: util-linux flock's usage and argument diagnostics and status 64, word for word.
cases.script:
flock || echo rc=$?
flock -x || echo rc=$?
flock --bogus || echo rc=$?
flock -Z || echo rc=$?
flock -w || echo rc=$?
flock --wait || echo rc=$?
flock -w x lock true || echo rc=$?
flock abc || echo rc=$?
flock -E x lock true || echo rc=$?
flock -E 300 lock true || echo rc=$?
flock -o -F lock true || echo rc=$?
flock -c true lock || echo rc=$?
flock lock -c || echo rc=$?
flock 2147483648 || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: G131: util-linux wording and statuses for an unopenable lock file (66), a closed descriptor (65) and a command that cannot be run (69), with and without -F.
cases.script:
flock missing/x true || echo rc=$?
exec 7>&-
flock 7 || echo rc=$?
flock lock ./nosuch-cmd || echo rc=$?
flock -F lock ./nosuch-cmd || echo rc=$?
flock lock -- true || echo rc=$?
printf 'after\n'

cases.purpose: G131: --opt=value, unambiguous prefixes, --nb, --fcntl, --timeout, -u with a command (it still runs), a directory as lock file, and options ending at FILE.
cases.script:
flock --timeout=1 lock true && echo timeout
flock --wait=1 lock true && echo wait
flock --conflict-exit-code=3 lock true && echo cec
flock --nb lock true && echo nb
flock --no-f lock true && echo nofork
flock --fcntl lock true && echo fcntl
flock -u lock echo unlock-runs
mkdir d
flock d echo dir
flock -s d echo shared
flock -n lock -E 5 true || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: G131: --fcntl takes an open-file-description lock; a second description conflicts with the conflict exit code.
cases.script:
exec 8>lock
flock --fcntl 8
flock --fcntl -n -E 5 lock true || echo rc=$?
flock --fcntl -u 8
flock --fcntl -n lock true && echo free
